description: Verify one build of a third-party kit — no game needed — against the core it is meant for (modules: a folder of kit modules, e.g. <exported game>/runtime-rust/kit-modules): the version of the contract and of every interface it consumes, then the structures of the contract, each compared with the core's. Answers ok, mode (isolated or common), contract { expected, found }, structs { expected, found } and the issues, each naming what was expected and what was found. Guide: gripforge_docs { topic: "kit-third-party" }.

kit.description: Absolute path of the output folder of gripforge_third_party_kit_build (it holds build.json): the build of the trust asked is taken from it. Use this, or wasm + manifest.

manifest.description: Its .kit.json: absolute path, or an http(s) URL.

modules.description: Absolute path of the folder of kit modules (kit-modules.json) whose core the build is checked against.

trust.description: How far the game trusts this kit. "isolated" (default): the kit keeps a memory of its own and cannot read or corrupt the game — use it for any kit you did not write. "common": the kit is placed in the memory of the core and of the other kits, as a GripForge kit is — faster, and NOT isolated: only for a kit the maker of the game trusts. The build declared must be the one of that mode.

wasm.description: The kit module: absolute path of the .wasm, or an http(s) URL (with manifest).

name: gripforge_third_party_kit_verify_build
title: Verify one build of a kit against a core
